mainTopic: Damage to the male organ and marriage into the קהל; a wounded כהן and marrying a נתינה
overview: This amud continues the laws of a man whose organ was damaged, which can bar him from marrying into the קהל. רב פפי insists that semen which does not exit through its proper place cannot cause conception. שמואל rules that a hole at the עטרה which healed closed makes the man unfit only if an emission would tear it open again. The גמרא then discusses how to test this, and a ברייתא adds that once such a hole closes, the man becomes fit again. אביי gives a remedy to help a small hole heal. רבא rules that the הלכה follows neither רבה בר רב הונא, who disqualified a man who urinates from two places, nor his father רב הונא, who disqualified נשים המסוללות from marrying a כהן. A new משנה teaches that a פצוע דכא and a כרות שפכה may marry a convert or a freed maidservant. The גמרא then asks about a wounded כהן. That leads to a debate over why a wounded man may marry a נתינה and whether marriage with gentiles takes effect at all. The debate continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב פפי rejects a lenient view: semen outside its place cannot cause conception
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי finishes rejecting רב ביבי's lenient view. Semen that comes out through its proper place can cause conception, but semen that comes out somewhere else cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the 'cut-short' family, you say 'cut-short' (weak) things? When it comes out in its proper place, it causes conception. When it does not come out in its proper place, it does not cause conception.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רב פפי's sharp rejection of a lenient ruling from the end of the previous daf. He explains that semen exiting from the wrong place cannot lead to children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפי's main point is about how conception works. Only semen that comes out through its normal place can lead to conception. So a man whose semen exits elsewhere is treated like one who cannot father children, and he remains unfit for the קהל.

keyTerms.meaning: From the 'cut-short' people, a play on words about a family whose members were said to die young
It 'ripens', meaning it can cause conception

phrases.english: From the 'cut-short' family, you say 'cut-short' words?
phrases.notes: A wordplay. רב פפי is teasing that someone from a short-lived family is saying 'short' (weak) ideas.

phrases.english: In its place, it causes conception;
not in its place, it does not cause conception.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמּוּלָאֵי, אָמְרִיתוּ מִילֵּי מוּלְיָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the argument carried over from the previous daf.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the lenient ruling that a man whose semen exits from a different spot is fit.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores that semen exiting outside its proper place cannot cause conception.

steps.title: שמואל's rule on a hole that healed closed
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules about a hole in the organ that closed up. If an emission would tear it open again, the man is unfit. Otherwise he is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: If it was pierced and then closed up, then in any case where an emission of semen would tear it open, he is unfit. If not, he is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling begins. שמואל gives a test for a hole that healed over: does the closure hold during an emission?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Healing alone is not enough. The closure must be strong enough to survive an emission. If it would tear open, the semen would again exit from the wrong place, so he is פסול. If the closure holds, he is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Was pierced and then closed up
He has an emission of semen
Unfit / fit (here, to enter the קהל)

steps.whyThisMatters: This test is the basis for everything that follows: where the hole must be, and how to check it.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
If it was pierced and closed up,
any case where, if he had an emission, it would tear, he is unfit.
And if not, he is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ruling on a related case: a hole that has healed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A healed hole makes him unfit only if an emission would tear it open again.

steps.title: רבא asks where the hole is located
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks where on the organ שמואל's case is. It cannot be below the עטרה, because there even a complete cut would leave him fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא discussed it: Where is this? If you say it is below the עטרה, then even if it was cut off completely he would also be fit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא questions שמואל's ruling to pin down exactly where the hole is. He rules out one possible location, which sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the hole were below the עטרה, the ruling would make no sense. Even cutting off that part entirely does not make a man unfit, so a mere hole there could not matter. The case must therefore be somewhere else.

phrases.english: Rava discussed it: Where?
If we say it is below the corona,
even if it was cut off he would also be fit,

steps.triggerLanguage: הָוֵי בֵּהּ רָבָא: הֵיכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact location in שמואל's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where on the organ is the hole in שמואל's case?

steps.title: The hole is at the corona itself
steps.stepSummary: רבא concludes that שמואל's case is a hole at the עטרה itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is at the עטרה itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own question. Since below the עטרה is ruled out, שמואל must mean a hole right at the עטרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the עטרה itself, damage can matter, so whether the closure holds makes a real difference. That is why שמואל's test applies there.

phrases.english: Rather, it is in the corona itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בַּעֲטָרָה עַצְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question from the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The hole is at the עטרה itself.

steps.title: A second report of שמואל confirms רבא's reading
steps.stepSummary: Another chain of rabbis reports שמואל's ruling with the words 'at the עטרה itself' stated outright, confirming רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רב מרי בר מר said that מר עוקבא said that שמואל said: If it was pierced at the עטרה itself and closed up, then in any case where an emission would tear it, he is unfit. If not, he is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רבא. A different report of שמואל's ruling says outright what רבא worked out by reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording is the same as the first report, except that it adds 'at the עטרה itself.' This shows that רבא's reasoning matches what שמואל actually said.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (introduces support from another report)

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's 'healed hole' rule applies to a hole at the עטרה itself. If an emission would tear it open, he is unfit. If not, he is fit.

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מָרִי בַּר מָר אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Mari bar Mar said that Mar Ukva said that Shmuel said:
If it was pierced in the corona itself and closed up,
any case where, if he had an emission, it would tear, he is unfit;
and if not, he is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's answer with an explicit report.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's reading that the hole is at the עטרה itself.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב מרי בר מר's report of שמואל's words in the name of מר עוקבא.

steps.title: How do we test whether the closure holds?
steps.stepSummary: רבא son of רבה asks רב יוסף for the practical way to check this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא son of רבה sent to רב יוסף: Let our teacher teach us, what do we do?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the rule is clear, someone asks the practical question: how do we actually check whether the hole would tear open?
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's rule depends on what would happen during an emission. That raises the question of how a בית דין can find out.

keyTerms.meaning: He sent to him (a written question)
What do we do? How do we act?

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רָבָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה לְרַב יוֹסֵף:
phrases.english: Rava, son of Rabba, sent to Rav Yosef:
Let our teacher teach us, what do we do?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רָבָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה לְרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rule itself to how it is checked in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical method for testing whether the closure would tear during an emission.

steps.title: רב יוסף's method using warm barley bread
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers: place warm barley bread on the man's body as described, which brings about an emission, and then observe what happens.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We bring warm barley bread and place it on his rear opening. He has an emission, and we look at it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a practical test. Warmth brings about an emission, and then they look to see whether the hole stays closed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method creates the exact situation שמואל's rule talks about, so the result can be seen directly. If the closure holds, he is כשר. If it tears, he is פסול.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַיְיתִינַן נַהֲמָא חַמִּימָא דִּשְׂעָרֵי,
phrases.english: He said to him: We bring warm barley bread,
and place it on his rear opening,
and he has an emission, and we observe it.
phrases.notes: 'Observe it' means checking whether the hole stays closed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַיְיתִינַן נַהֲמָא חַמִּימָא דִּשְׂעָרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the practical question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Use warm barley bread to bring about an emission, then check the closure.

steps.title: אביי: no special method is needed
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that not everyone is like יעקב אבינו, who never had an emission. An ordinary man is easily brought to an emission, so רב יוסף's extreme method is unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Is everyone like יעקב אבינו, about whom it is written 'my strength and the first of my vigor,' meaning he never had an emission in his life?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's method. A normal man is not like יעקב, so something much milder is enough to bring on an emission. This sets up אביי's own suggestion in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is understood to mean that ראובן came from יעקב's very first drop of seed, so יעקב never had an emission before. Only someone like יעקב would need such a drastic method to bring one about. Ordinary men are aroused far more easily, so warm bread is unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (a rhetorical challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not disputing שמואל's rule about the hole. He only rejects the need for רב יוסף's special method of checking.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אַטּוּ כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ הֲוַאי,
phrases.english: Abaye said: Is everyone like our forefather Jacob,
about whom it is written: 'My strength and the first of my vigor,'
meaning that he never had an emission in his life!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אַטּוּ כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רב יוסף's method is necessary.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the need for the artificial testing method, not שמואל's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The method is far stronger than needed. Only someone like יעקב would require it, while an ordinary man is brought to an emission much more easily.

steps.title: אביי suggests colored clothing instead
steps.stepSummary: After rejecting the barley-bread method, אביי offers a different way to bring about an emission: pass colored women's clothing in front of the man.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: We pass colored clothing in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his own replacement method for checking the man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8 אביי said ordinary men don't need warm bread to have an emission. He still wants a way to make the emission happen so it can be observed. His answer is to arouse the man by showing him colorful clothing.

keyTerms.meaning: we pass in front of him

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
We pass colored garments before him.
phrases.notes: These are women's colorful clothes, meant to arouse him so we can watch what happens at the emission.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אָמַר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יוסף's method, which אביי rejected in step 8
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to bring about an emission in order to check the man
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Pass colored women's clothing before him

steps.title: רבא: not everyone is ברזילי
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects אביי's method because most men are not aroused just by seeing clothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Is everyone like ברזילי הגלעדי?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down אביי's suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's method only works on a man who is easily aroused. רבא uses ברזילי הגלעדי as the example of such a man and says most people are not like that. So colored clothing cannot be relied on as a check.

keyTerms.meaning: is that to say? (a 'no way' question)
Barzilai the Gileadite, the example here of a man easily aroused

phrases.english: Rava said:
Is that to say that everyone
is Barzilai the Gileadite?!
phrases.notes: His point: most men won't get aroused just from seeing clothes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אַטּוּ כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's alternative method
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It only works on unusually easily aroused men, not on ordinary people

steps.title: Back to the first method
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the original method, רב יוסף's warm barley bread, is the right one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear as we answered at the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion by going back to the first answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both attacks are now settled. אביי's clothing idea failed, so we use רב יוסף's barley bread. It may not be needed for everyone, but it works for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: as we answered at the start

steps.whatToRemember: The check for a hole at the עטרה uses רב יוסף's warm barley bread method.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear
as we answered at first.
phrases.notes: This means רב יוסף's warm barley bread from step 7.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מְחַוַּורְתָּא כִּדְשַׁנִּין מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting אביי's idea, returns to רב יוסף's method
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We use the barley-bread method even though not everyone needs it

steps.title: A punctured member makes him unfit, and closing it makes him fit
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a punctured אבר makes a man unfit. If the hole closes up, he becomes fit again.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If it was punctured, he is unfit because his seed drips out. If it closed up, he is fit because he can father children. This is a case of an unfit person who becomes fit again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a new rule about a hole that heals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for being unfit is that the seed drips out weakly and cannot produce children. Once the hole closes, that reason is gone, so the man is fit again. The ברייתא points out that this is an unusual case where a פסול can be undone.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that this פסול depends on whether he can have children, so when that ability comes back, the פסול goes away.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If it was punctured, he is unfit,
because [his seed] drips out.
If it closed up, he is fit,
because he can father children.
And this is an unfit one who returns to his fitness.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: נִיקַּב — פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New ברייתא on the topic of a hole in the אבר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A punctured אבר makes him פסול. If it closes, he is כשר again.

steps.title: What does the word 'this' exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word 'זהו' in the ברייתא is meant to leave out.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'This' comes to exclude what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא zooms in on one word of the ברייתא and asks why it is there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'זהו' sounds limiting, as if only this case goes from unfit back to fit. So the גמרא asks which other case it means to exclude.

phrases.english: "This" comes to exclude what?

steps.triggerLanguage: ״זֶהוּ״ לְמַעוֹטֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in the ברייתא

steps.title: It excludes a membrane on a lung
steps.stepSummary: 'זהו' excludes a membrane that grew over a wound on an animal's lung, which does not count as a real covering.
steps.simpleTranslation: To exclude a membrane that grew because of a wound on the lung, which is not a real membrane.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word leaves out a case from animal law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hole in the אבר that closes really heals. A membrane that forms over a wound in a lung is weak and does not count as closing the hole. So in that case the earlier problem stays.

phrases.english: To exclude a membrane
that formed because of a wound on the lung,
phrases.notes: This is an animal's lung, from the laws of טריפות.

phrases.english: which is not a [real] membrane.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַעוֹטֵי קְרוּם שֶׁעָלָה מֵחֲמַת מַכָּה בָּרֵיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about 'זהו'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It excludes a wound-membrane on a lung, which does not count as a real covering

steps.title: How do we heal the hole?
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין asks אביי what practical steps make such a hole close up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי בר אבין sent to אביי: What do we do?
steps.whatsHappening: Since a closed hole makes him fit again, the גמרא now asks how to make the hole close.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said a closed hole makes the man fit. That raises a practical question: is there a way to help the hole heal? This line sets up אביי's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: he sent to him (a question by message)

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin sent to Abaye:
What do we do?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין לְאַבָּיֵי: הֵיכִי עָבְדִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Practical follow-up to the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A method for healing the hole

steps.title: אביי's healing remedy
steps.stepSummary: אביי describes the remedy: scratch the area with barley, rub in fat, let a large ant bite, then cut off the ant's head.
steps.simpleTranslation: We bring a barley grain and scratch the area, bring fat and rub it on, bring a large ant and let it bite, and cut off its head.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers with a step-by-step remedy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Scratching and the ant bite cause bleeding and new flesh, which closes the hole. The fat helps the area heal. Cutting off the ant's head keeps it stuck in place.

phrases.english: We bring a barley grain and scratch [the area] with it,
and we bring fat and rub it on,
and we bring a large ant
and let it bite him,
and we cut off its head.
phrases.notes: The ant's head stays clamped in place while the spot heals.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַיְיתִינַן שְׂעָרְתָּא וּמְסָרְטִינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אידי בר אבין
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Barley scratch, fat, an ant bite, and cutting off the ant's head

steps.title: Two limits on the remedy
steps.stepSummary: The remedy must use barley, not iron, because iron causes inflammation. It only works for a small hole, since a large one will peel open again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Specifically a barley grain, but iron causes inflammation. And this applies to a small hole, but a large one will peel off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds two details that limit when and how the remedy works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, the tool must be barley, because scratching with iron inflames the wound. Second, the remedy only helps a small hole. Over a large hole, the new skin will not hold and peels away.
steps.whatToRemember: A hole that closes makes the man fit again. The remedy uses barley, not iron, and only works on a small hole.

phrases.english: And specifically a barley grain,
but iron causes inflammation.
And this applies to a small [hole],
but a large one will peel off.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדַוְקָא שְׂעָרְתָּא, אֲבָל פַּרְזְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds limits to אביי's remedy
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Use barley, not iron. The remedy works only on a small hole.

steps.title: Urinating from two places makes him unfit
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא rules that a man who urinates from two openings is unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: One who urinates from two places is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling: a second opening that urine comes out of makes the man unfit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר רב הונא treats a second opening like the hole discussed above. So he makes the man פסול from entering the קהל.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
One who urinates from two places is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא: הַמֵּטִיל מַיִם מִשְּׁתֵּי מְקוֹמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New ruling related to holes in the אבר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who urinates from two places is פסול

steps.title: רבא: the הלכה follows neither son nor father
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the הלכה follows neither רבה בר רב הונא, on urinating from two places, nor his father רב הונא, who said נשים המסוללות are unfit for כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה is not like the son and not like the father. The son is what we just said. The father is what רב הונא said: women who rub against one another are unfit for כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the final halacha and rejects two rulings, one from a son and one from his father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Against the son: urinating from two places does not make a man פסול. Against the father: רב הונא made נשים המסוללות forbidden to a כהן. רבא says this behavior does not make them forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: women who rub against one another

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the son and father argue with each other. They made two separate rulings on different topics, and רבא rejects both.
steps.whatToRemember: הלכה: urinating from two places does not make a man פסול, and נשים המסוללות are not forbidden to a כהן.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: לֵית הִלְכְתָא לָא כִּבְרָא וְלָא כְּאַבָּא,
phrases.english: The halacha is not like the son and not like the father.
The son: that which we just said.
The father: as Rav Huna said:
Women who rub against one another
are unfit for the priesthood.
phrases.notes: רב הונא means they can't marry a כהן. רבא disagrees.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לֵית הִלְכְתָא לָא כִּבְרָא וְלָא כְּאַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבה בר רב הונא's ruling and also his father's ruling
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Urinating from two places is not פסול, and נשים המסוללות are not forbidden to a כהן

steps.title: Even רבי אלעזר would not call such a woman a זונה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up רבא's ruling against רב הונא. Even according to the strict view of רבי אלעזר, a זונה is only made through relations with a man. Lewd behavior between women is only פריצותא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even according to רבי אלעזר, who said that an unmarried man who has relations with an unmarried woman without intending marriage makes her a זונה, that only applies to a man. Between two women it is just immodest behavior.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why we do not follow רב הונא, who said נשים המסוללות are unfit for כהונה. Even the strictest opinion about who counts as a זונה would not include them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר is very strict: he says even ordinary relations outside marriage make a woman a זונה. But his rule is about relations with a man. What happens between two women is only פריצותא, so the woman stays permitted to a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman forbidden to a כהן because of forbidden relations
Immodest or lewd behavior, which is not a formal status

steps.whatToRemember: נשים המסוללות are permitted to a כהן. Even according to רבי אלעזר, only relations with a man can make a woman a זונה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the topic of who becomes disqualified from marrying a כהן before the new משנה begins.

phrases.english: And even according to Rabbi Elazar, who said:
an unmarried man who has relations with an unmarried woman
not for the sake of marriage makes her a zona
that applies only to a man,
but with a woman, it is mere licentiousness.
phrases.notes: This is going back to רב הונא's case from step 19, the נשים המסוללות.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רבא's rejection of רב הונא in step 19
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lewd behavior between women does not create זונה status, even according to רבי אלעזר

steps.title: משנה: Wounded men may marry a convert or a freed maidservant
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that a פצוע דכא and a כרות שפכה may marry a גיורת or a משוחררת. They are only forbidden to marry into the קהל, meaning a woman born Jewish.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man with crushed testicles and a man whose organ is cut off may marry a convert or a freed maidservant. They are only forbidden from entering the congregation, as the פסוק says: 'A man with crushed testicles or a severed organ shall not enter the congregation of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the limits of the prohibition on men with these injuries.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק forbids them only from coming into the 'קהל ה׳', the community of born Jews. A convert and a freed maidservant are not counted as part of that קהל for this purpose, so these men may marry them.

keyTerms.meaning: A man whose testicles are crushed or wounded
A man whose organ has been cut off
To enter the congregation, meaning to marry a woman born Jewish

steps.confusionAlert: 'Entering the קהל' does not mean coming into a shul or a gathering. It means marrying a woman born Jewish.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A man with crushed testicles and one whose organ is severed
are permitted to a female convert and a freed maidservant,
and they are forbidden only from entering the congregation,
as it is stated: "A man with crushed testicles shall not enter
nor one with a severed organ, into the congregation of the Lord."

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ פְּצוּעַ דַּכָּא וּכְרוּת שׇׁפְכָה מוּתָּרִין בְּגִיּוֹרֶת וּמְשׁוּחְרֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פצוע דכא and a כרות שפכה may marry a גיורת or a משוחררת. They are barred only from a woman born Jewish.

steps.title: What about a כהן with crushed testicles?
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת is asked whether a כהן who is a פצוע דכא may marry a convert or a freed maidservant. The question is whether he still has his special holiness or has lost it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רב ששת: a כהן with crushed testicles, may he marry a convert or a freed maidservant? Does he keep his holiness and stay forbidden, or does he lose his holiness and become permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question on the משנה. It asks how the rule works for a כהן with this injury.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A healthy כהן may not marry a convert because of his extra holiness. The question is whether the injury removes that holiness. If it does, he would be like any wounded Israelite, who the משנה says may marry her.

keyTerms.meaning: He remains in his state of holiness

phrases.english: GEMARA: They asked Rav Sheshet:
a priest with crushed testicles, what is the law
regarding a convert or a freed maidservant?
Does he remain in his holiness and is forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא לָאו בִּקְדוּשְׁתֵּיהּ קָאֵי וּשְׁרֵי?
phrases.english: or perhaps he does not remain in his holiness and is permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת: פְּצוּעַ דַּכָּא כֹּהֵן מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the משנה's rule to the case of a כהן
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a כהן who is a פצוע דכא keeps his priestly holiness and stays forbidden to a convert

steps.title: רב ששת proves from a ברייתא that the injury removes his holiness
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת cites a ברייתא: a wounded Israelite may marry a נתינה. If he had kept his holiness, the פסוק 'לא תתחתן בם' would forbid it. So the injury removes his former holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: You already learned it. A wounded Israelite may marry a Gibeonite woman. If you think he keeps his holiness, the פסוק 'You shall not marry with them' would apply here.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question with a proof from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A healthy Jew may not marry a נתינה. The ברייתא still lets a wounded Israelite marry her. This shows the injury removes his Jewish marriage-holiness. By the same reasoning, a wounded כהן also loses his priestly holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: You already learned it, in a ברייתא
A woman descended from the Gibeonites, normally forbidden to marry a Jew
If it enters your mind, if you think
'You shall not marry with them', the prohibition on marrying the nations of כנען

steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת's proof: a פצוע דכא may marry a נתינה, so it seems he has lost his former holiness, and a wounded כהן would lose his too. The next step shows that רבא rejects this proof.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב ששת's proof rests on the idea that 'לא תתחתן בם' is about holiness. That is exactly the assumption רבא attacks in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said to them: You already learned it:
an Israelite with crushed testicles
is permitted to a Gibeonite woman.
And if you think he remains in his holiness,
apply here "You shall not marry with them."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת, תְּנֵיתוּהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22 with a ברייתא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A פצוע דכא does not keep his former holiness, since he may marry a נתינה. So a wounded כהן seems to lose his priestly holiness too.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that permits a wounded Israelite to marry a נתינה

steps.title: רבא: The verse is about idolatry, not holiness
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects רב ששת's proof. The ban 'לא תתחתן בם' was never about holiness. It was about the fear that a child of the marriage will turn to idol worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Is the prohibition there about holiness or lack of holiness? No. The worry is that he will have a son who will go and worship idols.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רב ששת's proof from the previous step. He says the reason behind 'לא תתחתן בם' has nothing to do with holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת assumed that if the wounded man still had his holiness, 'לא תתחתן בם' would forbid him to marry a נתינה. רבא says that verse is driven by a different worry: children raised to worship idols. So the ברייתא allowing the marriage proves nothing about holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (a rhetorical question that rejects an assumption)
'Do not marry with them': the ban on marrying the nations of כנען

phrases.english: Rava said:
Is that to say that there, it is because of holiness
phrases.notes: 'There' means the פסוק 'לא תתחתן בם' that רב ששת used in his proof.

phrases.english: or lack of holiness?
Rather, perhaps he will father a son,
and that son will go and worship idols.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבא: אטו התם משום קדושה ולאו קדושה הוא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof רב ששת brought in step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the ברייתא of the wounded Israelite marrying a נתינה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It wrongly assumes that 'לא תתחתן בם' is about holiness, when it is really about the danger of idolatry.

steps.title: The ban on converted נתינים is only rabbinic, and only for men who can have children
steps.stepSummary: The Torah's worry applies only while they are gentiles. Once they convert they are permitted. The רבנן added a decree, but only for people who can have children, so it does not cover a פצוע דכא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only while they are gentiles. Once they convert, they are permitted, and it is the Rabbis who decreed against them. And when the Rabbis decreed, it was for those who can have children. This man cannot have children, so the Rabbis did not decree against him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now explains why the wounded man may marry a נתינה, without using the idea of lost holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, converted נתינים are allowed. Their ban is a rabbinic decree. That decree was aimed only at men who could father children, so a man who cannot have children was never included.

phrases.english: And this applies only while they are gentiles;
when they convert, they are permitted,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets ('to a Jew'); the word in square brackets is the corrected wording ('permitted').

phrases.english: and it is the Rabbis who decreed against them.
And when the Rabbis decreed against them,
it was for those who are able to have children;
but this one, who is not able to have children,
the Rabbis did not decree against him.

steps.triggerLanguage: והני מילי בגויותן כי מגיירי מישרא שרו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבא's own reason for the ברייתא, replacing the holiness reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the rabbinic decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wounded man may marry a נתינה only because he lost his holiness.
steps.terutzMaskana: He may marry her because the rabbinic decree never covered men who cannot have children.

steps.title: Challenge: then a ממזר should be forbidden to marry a נתינה
steps.stepSummary: If the decree covers anyone who can have children, a ממזר should be forbidden to a נתינה. But a משנה says ממזרים and נתינים may marry each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, a ממזר, who can have children, should also be forbidden! But we learned: ממזרים and נתינים are permitted to marry one another!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's explanation using a case it does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבא's rule, having children is what triggers the decree. A ממזר can have children, yet a משנה explicitly lets him marry a נתינה. So 'ability to have children' cannot be the dividing line.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so... (introduces a problem that follows from your logic)
A child of a forbidden union, who may not marry into the קהל
But we learned in a משנה...

phrases.english: But if so, a ממזר,
who is able to have children,
would he also be forbidden?
But we learned in a משנה:
ממזרים and נתינים
are permitted to marry one another!

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא מעתה ממזר דבר אולודי הכי נמי דאסיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'able to have children' line drawn in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the decree applies to anyone able to have children.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ממזר can have children, yet the משנה permits him to a נתינה, so the dividing line must be something else.

steps.title: The decree covers only people of proper lineage
steps.stepSummary: The rabbinic decree against נתינים applies only to כשרים. It does not apply to people who are already פסולים, like a ממזר or a פצוע דכא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: when the Rabbis decreed, it was for people of proper lineage. For disqualified people, the Rabbis did not decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces the 'can have children' rule with a new line: proper lineage versus disqualified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the ממזר case fits, since he is פסול and so not covered by the decree. The פצוע דכא is also פסול from the קהל, so he too may marry a נתינה.

keyTerms.meaning: People of proper lineage, fit to marry into the קהל
People disqualified from marrying into the קהל

phrases.english: Rather: when the Rabbis decreed,
it was for those of proper lineage.
For the disqualified, the Rabbis did not decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא כי גזור רבנן בכשרים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26 by redefining the scope of the decree.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The decree covers anyone able to have children.
steps.terutzMaskana: The decree covers only כשרים, so פסולים like a ממזר or a פצוע דכא may marry a נתינה.

steps.title: רבא retracts: the verse must speak of after conversion
steps.stepSummary: רבא takes back his claim that 'לא תתחתן בם' applies only to gentiles. Marriage with a gentile does not take effect at all. Only after conversion can there be marriage, so that is when the ban applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא then said: What I said is not correct. While they are gentiles, there is no marriage with them at all. Once they convert, there is marriage with them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects his own earlier claim from step 25 that the Torah ban only applies while they are gentiles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'marry' (חתנות) only makes sense where a marriage can take effect. Marriage with a gentile never takes effect. So the Torah's 'do not marry them' must refer to after they convert.

keyTerms.meaning: He then said again (changing his earlier view)
It is nothing; that statement is not correct
Marriage that takes effect, marriage ties

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not taking back the conclusion that the פצוע דכא may marry a נתינה. He is only taking back his claim that the Torah's ban applies only to gentiles.

phrases.english: Rava then said:
It is not correct (what I said);
while they are gentiles, there is no marriage with them;
once they convert, there is marriage with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הדר אמר רבא לאו מילתא היא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא retracts the premise 'והני מילי בגויותן' from step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the claim that the Torah ban applies just to gentiles.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is no marriage with gentiles, so a ban on 'marrying' them would be meaningless.

steps.title: רב יוסף: שלמה 'married' בת פרעה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges רבא from the פסוק saying שלמה married בת פרעה. That seems to show that marriage with a gentile does exist.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: 'And שלמה married the daughter of פרעה, king of מצרים'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a פסוק to attack רבא's new claim that gentiles have no marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the very same word, ויתחתן, for שלמה and a gentile princess. That suggests marriage with a gentile can take effect, against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: And he married into (from the word חתנות)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef objected:
"And Shlomo married"
"the daughter of Pharaoh, king of Egypt"!

steps.triggerLanguage: מתיב רב יוסף ויתחתן שלמה את בת פרעה מלך מצרים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's retraction in step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that there is no חתנות with gentiles.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק calls שלמה's union with a gentile princess חתנות.

steps.title: He converted her first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שלמה converted בת פרעה before marrying her.
steps.simpleTranslation: He converted her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא: when שלמה married her, she was no longer a gentile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she converted first, the חתנות in the פסוק was with a convert. That fits רבא's rule perfectly.

phrases.english: He converted her.

steps.triggerLanguage: גיורי גיירה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge.
steps.terutzMaskana: שלמה married her after she converted.

steps.title: But converts were not accepted in the days of דוד and שלמה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. Converts were not accepted in the times of דוד and שלמה, so how could שלמה convert her?
steps.simpleTranslation: But they did not accept converts, neither in the days of דוד nor in the days of שלמה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer that שלמה converted בת פרעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known tradition that no converts were accepted under דוד and שלמה. If so, her conversion could not have happened, and the problem returns.

phrases.english: But they did not accept converts
neither in the days of David
nor in the days of Shlomo!

steps.triggerLanguage: והא לא קבלו גרים לא בימי דוד ולא בימי שלמה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שלמה converted בת פרעה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No conversions were accepted in שלמה's time.

steps.title: The reason was fear of converts seeking the king's table
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer. Converts were refused then only out of fear that they wanted to share in the royal power and wealth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the reason anything other than the table of kings?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by pointing to the reason converts were refused. This sets up the next move, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Converts were turned away because people might convert just to enjoy the king's table. Once the reason is known, the ban can be limited to cases where that reason applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Is the reason anything other than...? (a rhetorical question)
The table of kings: royal wealth and power

phrases.english: Is the reason anything
other than the table of kings?
phrases.notes: They worried people were converting just to share in the king's power and wealth.

steps.triggerLanguage: מידי הוא טעמא אלא לשולחן מלכים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to answer the challenge in step 31 by identifying the reason converts were not accepted.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the reason behind the rule, setting up a limit on it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No conversion at all was possible in שלמה's days.
steps.terutzMaskana: The refusal was based only on fear of people seeking royal benefits; the full answer continues on the next amud.
